text:
alex: quick sketch: reconcile local token-buckets across regions with delta-syncs instead of central lease pulls. trying to avoid central hot path but still allow global revokes. thoughts?

tara: curious how delta-sync avoids oscillation when a region suddenly sees a spike.

alex: idea is each region keeps a soft reserve and exchanges compact deltas every 100ms. if reserve drops below local-min, region enters conservative mode (reduce burst factor). deltas include monotonic counters + last-applied id.

ben: worry: with network partitions we could have split-brain where both regions burst using stale deltas. can we add a fast global kill switch for abuse?

alex: yes — global revoke channel (pubsub) that carries tenant-id + revoke-epoch. regions must check revoke-epoch on every admission decision. revoke supersedes deltas.

mila: what about fairness between tenants on a single shard? do we still track per-tenant EWMA or switch to a per-tenant proportional share window?

tara: proportional share makes accounting simpler for steady state, but EWMA helps when load changes quickly. perhaps hybrid: per-tenant target share + EWMA smoothing of observed usage.

alex: proto sketch (very rough):
```
message DeltaSync {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  uint64 epoch = 2; // monotonic
  int64 delta_tokens = 3;
  uint64 last_applied_id = 4;
}

message Revoke {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  uint64 revoke_epoch = 2; // higher = newer
}
```

ben: ops question: how do we ensure timely revoke delivery if pubsub lags? we need immediate local protection too.

mila: local protection = short probation window + aggressive backoff on errors. if a region sees high error counts or external abuse signals, it should immediately cut headroom for that tenant until revoke confirmed.

alex: tradeoffs: delta-sync reduces central load but increases probability of transient double-spend under partition. mitigation: conservative deltas (cap per-sync pull) + enforce global max-burst-per-tenant.

tara: can we simulate? i'd like scenarios: (A) region spike with 200ms delta lag, (B) pubsub delay 1s for revoke, (C) central offline. we should measure p50/p99 token overspend and recovery time.

deploy-bot: [ci-sim] queued: delta-sync/partition-suite. run id: sim-2026-03-23-42. results: pending. link: https://ci.internal/sim/2026-03-23-42

ben: next steps: alex write RFC with failure matrix + explicit revoke semantics, mila draft local probation heuristics, tara build sims & tie to chaos infra. can we aim to canary on staging next week?

alex: yes. i'll include cost estimate (bandwidth + CPU) vs central-lease approach. thanks all. :thumbsup:
